fields.headline: Someone I love is in a mental health crisis, and it keeps getting *harder*.
When you're holding someone up, you stop checking on *yourself*.
You become the calm one, while your own body has been quietly *screaming* for weeks.
Losing track of me didn't make me better for them. It made me *shakier*.
So before a hard room, I take a few minutes for me *first*.
I feel what's in my chest, and I look at it without *judging* it.
Then I set down what isn't mine. I can't do their healing *for* them.
Taking care of you isn't *selfish*. It's how you stay someone they can lean on.
Check in *first*.
fields.text: A few private minutes before the hard room: name what you're feeling, set down what isn't yours to carry, and walk in as yourself. There's an app for that.
